Chaos Theory Chest X-Ray Feature Analysis

Exploratory research investigating whether chaos-theory-derived numerical descriptors can capture subtle structural differences between NORMAL and PNEUMONIA chest X-ray images.

Research Context

Research question: Can chaos-theory-based numerical descriptors capture subtle differences in chest X-ray image structure between normal and pneumonia cases?

This dashboard represents the first stage of the research. Several candidate descriptors were investigated, while Fractal Dimension (FracDim) and Hurst exponent are the primary successfully usable chaos-theory numerical features highlighted in this stage.

The objective at this stage is exploratory feature characterization, not clinical diagnosis or prediction of terminal illness.

PCA of the Numerical Feature Space

Stage 1 Research Interpretation

Stage 1 — Exploratory Feature Analysis

The extracted numerical chaos features show a slight separation between NORMAL and PNEUMONIA observations despite the limited successfully usable chaos-feature space.

This is an encouraging exploratory observation, but the substantial overlap between classes means it should not be presented as a diagnostic classifier.

Next stage: expand the feature-extraction pipeline, investigate additional chaos descriptors, evaluate feature stability, and determine whether the observed separation persists under formal statistical testing and machine-learning evaluation.

Current Numerical Result

ClassMean FracDimMean Hurst
NORMAL 1.8639 0.7295
PNEUMONIA 1.8493 0.7313

The mean difference is small: FracDim differs by -0.0146 and Hurst differs by 0.0018. The value of the present stage is therefore in establishing whether chaos-derived numerical descriptors contain potentially useful information, rather than claiming strong classification performance.
